heading_degrees.units: degrees true, clockwise from north (treated as ground track)

scenarios.description: Straight-line dead-reckoning reference: ground speed x elapsed time along the supplied heading, interpreted as the ground track. Illustrative only.
assumptions: Heading is treated as the ground track (direction of motion over the ground).
Ground speed already includes wind; no wind correction is applied.
No turns, climbs, descents or speed changes after the last known position.

scenarios.description: Sensitivity check: the same distance flown along 150.0 degrees (-10 degrees from the supplied heading). Hypothetical.
assumptions: Same ground speed and elapsed time as the baseline; straight-line constant track.
Heading offset is a fixed sensitivity value, not a measured error.

scenarios.scenario_name: Hypothetical wind drift (speed treated as airspeed)
scenarios.description: HYPOTHETICAL: IF the supplied speed were airspeed along the supplied heading, the endpoint would be the baseline vector plus a wind drift of 15.0 nm toward 60 degrees. The input is defined as ground speed, so this is a sensitivity illustration only and is not part of the baseline or the search region.
assumptions: Supplied speed reinterpreted as true airspeed (contradicts the stated ground-speed input).
Wind constant in speed and direction for the whole elapsed time and at all altitudes.
Simple vector addition; no wind-correction angle or aircraft performance modelled.

properties.label: Illustrative search region
properties.area_note: Approximate: computed in the local AEQD projection, which is not equal-area.
properties.buffer_rule: buffer_nm_applied = max(position_uncertainty_nm, search_region_buffer_nm); the two are not summed.
properties.method: Convex hull (in a local azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the last known position) of the last known position, the baseline and +/-u heading-sensitivity endpoints, and arc points sampled every ~5 degrees across [h-u, h+u] at the baseline distance; then buffered by max(position_uncertainty_nm, search_region_buffer_nm).
properties.orientation: Exterior rings counter-clockwise (RFC 7946 right-hand rule); coordinates [longitude, latitude].
properties.disclaimer: Illustrative, non-operational region for demonstration only. It is NOT a probability contour, NOT a validated confidence region and NOT an operational search boundary. No land/water mask is applied, so the region may include land.

grid.ordering: Row-major. row 0 = northernmost, increasing southward; column 0 = westernmost, increasing eastward (in the local projection). cell_id = 'r{row}c{column}'.
grid.score_description: Relative visualization values in [0, 1] for demonstration only. They are NOT probabilities and carry no real-world meaning; a higher value does NOT mean a target is more likely to be in that cell. Computed as a Gaussian fall-off of the distance from each cell centre to the straight baseline track segment (sigma = 0.25 x the region's larger projected extent), set to 0 outside the region, then min-max normalised across all cells.

fuel_context.explanation: Reported fuel remaining: 40%. A percentage alone is insufficient to estimate endurance or range: that would need usable fuel capacity, fuel flow at the actual power setting and altitude, required reserves and aircraft-specific performance data. None of these are supplied, and SkyTrace AI does not invent them, so endurance is null and fuel does not change the geometry. The aircraft type is a descriptive label only.

wind_context.description: Wind 18 kt blowing FROM 240 degrees, i.e. TOWARD 60 degrees (true). Reported for context only; it is not added to the baseline because ground speed already reflects it.
limitations: Ground speed already includes the effect of wind, so wind is not applied to the baseline.
Separating wind from aircraft motion would require true airspeed and true heading, not ground speed.
Aircraft performance data (speeds, climb/descent, glide) is not modelled.
Altitude is unknown; wind varies strongly with altitude.
Winds are treated as constant; real winds vary in time and space.
Navigation mode (heading hold vs. track hold / autopilot) is unknown.
No track history (radar, ADS-B or other surveillance) is used.

explanation: Starting from the last known position (13.8000, 86.5000), a straight-line dead-reckoning reference covers 183.3 nm (220 kt ground speed for 50 min) along a ground track of 160 degrees true, reaching an illustrative baseline endpoint near (10.9137, 87.5618). To show sensitivity to heading, the same distance is swept from 150 to 170 degrees (+/-10 degrees). The illustrative search region is the convex hull of that swept sector and the start point, buffered by 10 nm, covering roughly 10,479 square nautical miles. Wind is shown for context but not added, because ground speed already reflects it; fuel percentage is reported but cannot bound the area without aircraft-specific data. Grid values are demonstration scores for visualization only. This is a hypothetical sketch, not an operational search plan.
assumptions: The heading is interpreted as the ground track (direction of motion over the ground), because it is combined with ground speed. With wind present, true heading and ground track differ.
Straight-line motion at constant ground speed from the last known position for the whole elapsed time.
Ground speed already includes wind; wind is reported as context and never added to the baseline.
Heading sensitivity scenarios use fixed offsets of +/-u (and capped +/-2u) degrees; they are not measured errors.
Distances use the WGS84 ellipsoid; 1 nm = 1852 m exactly.
Geometry is built in a local azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the last known position.
Fuel and aircraft type are descriptive context and do not alter any geometry.
warnings: No land/water mask is applied: the illustrative region and grid may include land.
Heading is treated as ground track together with ground speed; if the inputs are actually true heading or airspeed, the baseline is not representative.
Fuel percentage alone cannot determine endurance or range; no fuel-limited boundary is applied.
The search region is illustrative only: not a probability contour, not a validated confidence region and not an operational boundary.
Grid scores are demonstration values for visualization only and are not probabilities.
disclaimer: SkyTrace AI is a hackathon PROTOTYPE for demonstration and education. It does not locate any real aircraft, does not compute operational search-and-rescue statistics, and must not be used for real search planning. All regions, scenarios and scores are illustrative sensitivity sketches based on simplified assumptions. Real incidents must be handled by the responsible Rescue Coordination Centre using approved tools.
